evals.name: hang-deadlock-and-async
evals.prompt: Our .NET background service stopped processing work and we had to restart it. I grabbed a memory dump while it was stuck. Figure out why it hung.
evals.ground_truth: Two real stuck conditions: (a) a contended monitor — one background thread owns a lock another thread waits on (syncblk shows monitorHeld + owner + waitingThreadCount>=1); (b) an async method <WorkAsync>d__N suspended at await 0 on a never-completing task (dumpasync shows status 'suspended at await 0'). A correct diagnosis names at least one with cited evidence and does not claim a crash/exception caused it.
assertions: Classifies the symptom as a hang/deadlock or async stall, NOT a crash or memory leak
Cites concrete evidence: syncblk owner/waiter and/or a dumpasync 'suspended at await' machine
Names a correct root cause (contended monitor and/or parked async await)
Does not mistake the 3 preallocated runtime exceptions for the cause
Stays bounded: reaches a conclusion without re-running identical commands or exceeding ~12 scry commands

evals.name: under-determined-idle
evals.prompt: Users reported the app felt sluggish around 2pm. I took a dump a bit later. Can you tell me what was slow?
evals.ground_truth: The dump is of a healthy, idle process: no faulting thread, no contended monitors, no suspended async machines, no dominant heap type. The only exceptions are the 3 benign preallocated runtime singletons (empty message, carried by no thread). The pathological 'slowness' is not present in this snapshot. Correct outcome is INSUFFICIENT with a recommendation to capture a dump during the slowness or a CPU trace.
assertions: Reaches an INSUFFICIENT / not-enough-information conclusion rather than asserting a definite root cause
Explicitly recognizes the OutOfMemory/StackOverflow/ExecutionEngine exceptions as benign/preallocated and NOT the cause
Recommends the right next artifact (a dump taken during the slowness, and/or a CPU profiler/trace)
Stays bounded: does not loop or exceed the step budget chasing a non-existent cause

evals.name: memory-leak-static-cache
evals.prompt: This service's memory keeps climbing until it gets OOM-killed. Here's a dump taken when it was near the top. What's leaking?
evals.ground_truth: The heap is dominated by System.Byte[] (~350 MB, hundreds of 1 MB arrays), all retained (gcroot rooted:true via a strong handle to a long-lived array/collection). Correct diagnosis: an unbounded collection of byte[] is the leak; cite dumpheap --stat (byte[] dominant) and gcroot (rooted:true) as evidence.
assertions: Identifies System.Byte[] as the dominant heap type via dumpheap --stat
Runs gcroot on a representative object to establish it is retained (rooted:true)
Names the root cause as an unbounded/long-lived collection of byte[] (a leak), not transient pressure
Does not mistake the 3 preallocated runtime exceptions for the cause
Stays bounded: reaches the conclusion without re-running identical commands
